mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered quarters, or the negative rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) rising above 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) is flat or declining indicates labor market softening, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% AND (PAYEMS flat or declining for 2 months)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the interaction term's rank IC is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC drops below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and material sectors and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered events, or the negative rank IC is below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS below 3% for two consecutive months signals a mismatch between inflation and policy rate, creating policy uncertainty that elevates market volatility and reduces S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the interaction's rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in an expansionary regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 AND UNRATE < 3.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered months, or the positive rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 7% while consumption growth (GDPC1) is stagnant signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces near-term consumption demand and weighs on equities over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY > 7% AND GDPC1 YoY growth < 1% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the interaction's rank IC is below 0.02.
